profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed to Prime, most likely Prime Data Centers given the California and Texas registry locations. Prime Data Centers own site states the company was established in 2017 in California and is now headquartered at 400 North Ervay Street, Dallas, Texas, under founder and CEO Nicholas Laag, and describes itself as majority founder owned. The company reports 28 data centers across 13 campuses globally with a 4 plus gigawatt expansion pipeline, and lists Silicon Valley and Dallas among its confirmed North America markets, alongside Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Sacramento, matching both states where this registry lists a Prime facility. No building specific address, opening date, or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Prime Santa Clara in Santa Clara County, California, publishes 57 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet of technical space, operated by Prime.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 5700 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 1425 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Prime Santa Clara holds 3 published certifications: SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), ISO 27001 (a certified information security management system). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

California has 22 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 10 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 356 MW. Prime Santa Clara contributes 57 MW of that total. That is a meaningful facility by colocation standards, though still below the scale where frontier AI training clusters typically operate.
